header.title: Word Counter
header.description: Instant word, character, sentence, and paragraph counts for any text. See reading time, top keywords, and unique word frequency — all free.

input.ariaLabel: Text to count words and characters
input.placeholder: Start typing or paste your text here to see word count and other statistics...

realtime.title: Real-Time Counting
realtime.body: Every stat updates instantly as you type — no submit button needed. Words, characters, sentences, and paragraphs.

time.title: Reading & Speaking Time
time.body: Estimated reading time (200 wpm) and speaking time (130 wpm) are calculated automatically.

keywords.title: Top Keywords
keywords.body: The most frequent non-trivial words are shown with proportional frequency bars — useful for checking keyword density.

items.writers: Writers checking they meet or stay under a word limit for submissions
items.students: Students verifying essay length requirements before submitting
items.speakers: Podcasters or speakers estimating how long their script will take
items.seo: SEO writers checking keyword frequency and density
items.editors: Editors reviewing content length and reading complexity at a glance

items.blog: Average blog posts read in 7–10 minutes — aim for 1,400–2,000 words for that range.
items.keywords: Check the top keywords list to spot over-repetition before your editor does.
items.speaking: Speaking time assumes 130 wpm — adjust if you speak faster or slower in practice.
items.noSpaces: Use character count (no spaces) when working with platforms that count differently.

free.question: Is the word counter free?
free.answer: Yes, completely free. It uses no tokens and does not require an account or sign-in.

privacy.question: Is my text sent anywhere?
privacy.answer: No. All counting happens locally in your browser — your text never leaves your device and is not stored on our servers.

counts.question: What does it count?
counts.answer: Words, characters (with and without spaces), sentences, and paragraphs, plus estimated reading and speaking time and your most frequent keywords.

timing.question: How are reading and speaking time calculated?
timing.answer: Reading time assumes about 200 words per minute and speaking time about 130 words per minute, which are common average paces. Your actual pace may differ.

stopwords.question: Why do common words not appear in the keyword list?
stopwords.answer: Frequent function words like "the", "and", and "of" are filtered out so the keyword list reflects the words that actually characterize your text.
